content: Write a memo to staff about returning to the office three days a week.

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** All Staff
**FROM:** [Name], [Title]
**DATE:** [Date]
**RE:** Updated In-Office Schedule — Effective [Date]

---

Beginning **[Month Day]**, all staff will work from the office **three days per week**. I want to share the details, the reasoning behind the change, and what we're doing to make the transition as smooth as possible.

**The schedule**

- **Tuesday and Wednesday** will be company-wide anchor days. Everyone is in.
- Your **third day** will be set by your team, so you can align around the work that benefits most from being together. Managers will confirm their team's day by **[Date]**.
- Core hours in the office are **[10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.]**. Outside of those hours, your start and end times remain yours to manage.

**Why we're making this change**

Over the past [period], we've heard consistently — in engagement surveys, skip-levels, and manager feedback — that a few things have gotten harder: onboarding new colleagues, working across teams, and the kind of unplanned conversation that turns a good idea into a better one. Three days gives us enough shared time to rebuild that connective tissue while preserving real flexibility for focused work.

This is not a change based on concerns about productivity. Your work has been excellent, and that's not in question.

**What's changing on the logistics side**

- **Desks:** [Assigned seating returns for all staff / Hoteling continues; book through [system]]. You'll receive your assignment by [Date].
- **Parking and transit:** [Details — subsidy, garage access, shuttle schedule].
- **Food service:** The café will return to full hours, and [coffee service / breakfast on anchor days] will be available.
- **Meetings:** We're asking teams to keep collaborative work — planning, reviews, brainstorms — on in-office days, and to protect remote days for focused work. Meetings will remain video-enabled for colleagues who are remote or traveling.

**Exceptions and accommodations**

- Fully remote employees hired as remote are **not** affected by this change.
- If you have a medical need, caregiving responsibility, or other circumstance that makes this schedule difficult, please talk with your manager or reach out to [HR contact] directly. We will handle these conversations confidentially and in good faith.
- Occasional schedule adjustments — a delivery, an appointment, a sick child — don't require formal approval. Just let your manager know.

**What happens next**

- **[Date]:** Managers confirm team third days
- **[Date]:** Desk assignments and parking details distributed
- **[Date]:** New schedule takes effect
- **[Date]:** Check-in survey to hear how it's going

**A final note**

I know a change like this lands differently depending on your commute, your household, and how you work best. Some of you will welcome it; some of you won't. Both reactions are fair, and I'd rather hear your honest reaction than a polite one.

I'll host an open Q&A on **[Date] at [Time]** in **[location / link]**, and I'll be answering questions in **[channel]** through the end of the week. You can also submit questions anonymously at **[link]** — I'll address the common themes at the session.

Thank you for the flexibility and care you've shown through a lot of change. I don't take it for granted.

[Name]

---

Happy to adjust this — I can make the tone warmer or more directive, add a detailed FAQ, shorten it for email, or rework it if your policy differs (fixed days for everyone, manager discretion, phased rollout, etc.).
I want to see this written for a different reader than the first version. Rewrite it for a reader who already knows the background.
